name: AZERBAIJAN

flag.title: Flag of Azerbaijan
flag.note: Blue, red & green with crescent & star

lead: Azerbaijan is where Europe meets Asia, between the Caspian Sea and the Caucasus mountains. Gas leaks from the ground here and has burned for centuries. People call it the Land of Fire. Baku, the capital, mixes old stone towers with glass skyscrapers.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Snowy Caucasus mountains fill the north. The flat Absheron Peninsula juts into the Caspian Sea. The Caspian is the world's biggest lake, bigger than Germany.
Wet Talysh forests cover the south, with rare silkworm trees. Azerbaijan has nine of Earth's eleven climate zones in one small country.
animals: Caucasian leopards prowl the remote mountain forests. The Karabakh horse, bred here for over 2,000 years, is the national animal. It has a golden coat.
Flamingos gather on the Caspian mudflats each autumn. The Caspian seal lives nowhere else on Earth. Giant sturgeon, fish as big as small cars, once filled the sea.
culture: People drink black tea all day from pear-shaped armudu glasses. They hold a sugar cube between their teeth. UNESCO lists Azerbaijani carpet-weaving as world heritage.
Mugham is classical music. A singer makes up the tune on the spot over a tar lute for an hour. At Novruz, the spring New Year, streets fill with bonfires and painted eggs.
history: Fire temples drew Zoroastrians (people who honour fire) for thousands of years. Arab, Mongol, Persian, and Russian rulers each swept through. They left mosques and fortresses.
In the 1870s, Baku produced half the world's oil. Azerbaijan became independent in 1918, then again in 1991, when the Soviet Union (a huge Russia-led country) collapsed.
wows: Yanar Dağ hillside has burned nonstop since the 1950s, fuelled by gas from below.
Baku's Formula 1 car race roars past an 800-year-old walled city.
The Caspian holds about 90% of the world's wild sturgeon.
Baku's Flame Towers (glass skyscrapers) have 10,000 LED panels that show moving fire.
Gobustan's rocks hold 6,000+ carvings spanning up to 40,000 years.
Azerbaijan drilled an oil well in 1846, 13 years before the famous well in Pennsylvania, USA.
The Caspian lies about 28 metres below sea level, the lowest big lake surface on Earth.

myths.fact: Mud volcanoes burp out cool mud and gas instead. Azerbaijan has hundreds of them, about half of all on Earth.
They speak Azerbaijani, which is close to Turkish.
